findings.title: Advertised lane schema omits uniqueness constraint
findings.why_it_matters: MCP clients use the advertised JSON Schema to construct tool arguments. That schema accepts duplicate flow-node IDs, but runtime validation rejects the same request, so clients can submit schema-valid calls that deterministically fail before the lane mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the Zod duplicate-ID validation and add generated-schema support for `uniqueItems: true` on `add_lane.flowNodeIds`; add a parity assertion for that keyword.
evidence: src/server/tools.ts:224-227 rejects duplicates with `new Set(values).size === values.length`.
The generated `tools` schema for `flowNodeIds` contains only `type: array`, string `items`, and `minItems: 1`; it has no `uniqueItems: true`.
`parseToolRequest('add_lane', { poolId: 'p', name: 'lane', flowNodeIds: ['Task_1', 'Task_1'] })` throws `Flow node IDs must be unique`.

testing_gaps: No test asserts that the advertised add_lane flowNodeIds schema carries the duplicate-ID constraint accepted by runtime validation.
